title: Parallaft: Runtime-Based CPU Fault Tolerance via Heterogeneous Parallelism
problem: Increasing silicon faults in modern microprocessors create silent data corruption risks; existing software-based error detection suffers from high power and performance overhead, while state-of-the-art hardware fault-tolerance techniques are too complex for production deployment.
motivation: As fault rates increase with process scaling, efficient error detection mechanisms are essential for reliability; leveraging processor heterogeneity (little cores) to offload error checking reduces overhead while avoiding hardware complexity.
method: Parallaft repurposes insights from hardware heterogeneous-parallelism fault tolerance in pure software using modern OS tools: copy-on-write checkpointing, dirty-page tracking, and performance-counter synchronization. Error checking is offloaded to little cores of heterogeneous processors (e.g., Apple M2), achieving detection without dedicated hardware.
key_novelty: Adapting hardware heterogeneous fault-tolerance concepts to software-based implementation using OS primitives and little-core offloading on commodity heterogeneous processors.
contributions: A software-based error detection technique leveraging heterogeneous parallelism insights without hardware modifications
Using copy-on-write, dirty-page tracking, and performance-counter synchronization for efficient checking
Demonstration on Apple M2 achieving half the energy cost of homogeneous duplication (RAFT) while maintaining comparable performance
limitations: Evaluation limited to Apple M2 heterogeneous architecture; applicability to other heterogeneous processors and sensitivity to workload heterogeneity not discussed.
primary_theme: Software-based error detection via heterogeneous core offloading
